name: India
summary_text: India demands real caution from trans visitors, with a complex mix of constitutional protection and real practical gaps. The Supreme Court's 2014 NALSA judgment affirmed a constitutional right to self-determined gender identity, and the 2019 Act provides third-gender recognition. But a 2026 amendment bill — passed by parliament — has been called a "huge setback" by Human Rights Watch: it removes the self-identification right and narrows the legal definition. Police abuse is documented (a trans woman was groped by a railway-protection constable to "check gender"; TheProbe documents police atrocities), airport security discriminated against a trans student at Chennai (CISF), passport authorities have demanded unwarranted medical exams, and a new penal code removed safeguards protecting trans people from sexual violence. Enforcement is uneven — only 11 of 36 states and territories have transgender protection cells. India has no trans-murder toll comparable to Brazil and courts are protective, but the police abuse + amendment setback + safeguard removal + enforcement gaps + airport and passport friction place it in the middle of the scale. Huge subnational variation is expected: liberal metros like Bangalore and Kerala are materially safer than conservative rural north and central states.

sources.title: India’s Transgender Rights Bill a Huge Setback | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Mar 2026): 'India's Transgender Rights Bill a Huge Setback' — the government's amendment to the transgender-rights law rolls back protections for trans people.

sources.title: Transgender Bill: India parliament passes amendment to redefine transgender identity amid protests
sources.claim_summary: BBC (March 2026): India's parliament passed a controversial bill amending the 2019 Transgender Persons Act - changing how trans people are legally recognised and their right to self-identify; critics warn it could exclude many trans, non-binary and gender-fluid people. Context: the 2014 NALSA 'third gender' ruling, ~2 million trans people, and persistent discrimination in education, healthcare and employment.

Times of India (Aug 2024): a group of trans women heading to RG Kar Medical College filed an FIR alleging an RPF (railway police) constable groped one of them at Rabindra Sadan metro station, 'questioning her gender' - a 'gender check' as pretext for sexual assault.

sources.title: Transgender Persons Expose Police Abuse: "Gender Is Not in Genitals"
sources.claim_summary: The Probe (June 2024): transgender persons expose police abuse - first-person accounts of degrading treatment by authorities, including arrests by the RPF in Assam; 'gender is not in genitals'.

sources.title: Transgender student faces discriminatory treatment at Chennai airport
sources.claim_summary: New Indian Express (Nov 2024): trans law student Sakshi Jain was stopped by CISF personnel at Chennai airport Terminal 1 - despite presenting a PAN card and an official receipt showing her documentation update was underway, officers demanded both 'old' and 'new' ID cards and escalated the situation; highlights airport-screening discrimination against trans travellers in India.

sources.title: Trans Persons in India Fear Rise in Sexual Violence Under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita with Removal of Legal Safeguards - Frontline
sources.claim_summary: Frontline (Sept 2024): the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (replacing the Indian Penal Code) removed legal safeguards protecting the trans community from sexual violence - trans people fear rape with impunity; first-person accounts of harassment and assault.

sources.title: Country policy and information note: sexual orientation and gender identity and expression, India, December 2025 (accessible) - GOV.UK
sources.claim_summary: UK Home Office CPIN on sexual orientation and gender identity and expression in India (Dec 2025): official country-of-origin information for asylum claims - legal position, societal treatment, state protection.

NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 404 - page removed); the underlying SCC OnLine blog post (Feb 2026) covered the Allahabad High Court granting relief to a trans person asked to take a medical exam by passport authorities.

Madras High Court judgment (S. Sushma v Commissioner of Police, W.P.No.7284 of 2021, 7 June 2021, Justice N. Anand Venkatesh): landmark case brought by a same-sex couple harassed by police - the court's sweeping guidelines on protecting LGBTQIA+ persons, police sensitisation, banning conversion therapy, and directions to the National Medical Commission and education authorities.
